name: Light Cornflower Blue
lede: Light Cornflower Blue is a very light blue named for the cornflower, close enough to Sky Blue in our library that the two are almost interchangeable.

sections.title: Lighter than the flower
sections.body:
The library records Light Cornflower Blue from the ISCC-NBS system's 1955 block 199, and from the 1912 Ridgway atlas, plate VIII, hue 45, tone d [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[sky-blue]], [[pale-cerulean]], [[uranian-blue]] and [[sky]], at 2.5, 3.7, 
In LCH terms it measures lightness 79, chroma 23, hue 242 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "very light blue" block, Munsell 9.8B 7.9/5.7, between plain [[blue]] and [[azure-blue|Azure Blue]] [1]. The nearest named color in the library is [[sky-blue|Sky Blue]], about 2.5 units away by CIEDE2000, close enough that most people would call them the same color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in just 24 of 23,781 paintings, 0.1 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 14 [2]. That makes it rarer than 65 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, at 0.1 percent of that century's 8,345 paintings, 1.5 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a light, in 50 percent of its appearances [2].

The earliest match is dated 1425, by Sandro Botticelli; that is 487 years before the name's own first record, in 1912, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence of the actual paint, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
